rationale: The four-view mass is visually coherent as a single object, so repair integrity is high, but it is too generic and too isolated to satisfy the neighborhood_living brief. The dominant form reads as a simple cylindrical extrusion with small punctures and a lifted base, not as a capacity-aware street building with an active ground threshold and one clear public void or terrace. Across views the access edge does not resolve into a legible public response; the blue frontage is met by a nearby object, not by a court, seam, undercut, or entry gesture. The form also has weak hierarchy: there is no distinct public base and no upper mass differentiation beyond slight lifting. It is coherent in isolation but semantically misaligned with the program and with the reference set, which all rely on either a voided center, a stepped/tapered hierarchy, or a clearly active ground condition.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is far more monotone and cylindrical; it lacks the sectional taper and base articulation shown here.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped/tapered upper mass with a clear dominant body and a legible street-facing base can support mixed-use hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is a rectilinear block with a strong atrium void; the candidate is a sealed punctured cylinder with no comparable public void.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A carved central void can create public legibility and daylight while keeping the main mass coherent.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate shows no meaningful access-facing cut, canopy, or ground response.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A small commercial mass can express an active ground threshold through a canopy, seam, or entry fold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate does not develop a surrounding courtyard or inhabited terrace sequence; only the loose idea of an isolated mass is transferable.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/courtyard living can preserve a clear ground-waterfront relationship while varying upper massing.

warnings: Parcel containment could not be deterministically confirmed from this image alone because the green boundary appears adjacent but the mass does not clearly establish a robust relationship to it.
The access edge is not answered with a legible public threshold; the blue frontage remains semantically unused.
The form is coherent in all views, but coherence alone is insufficient here because the program contract requires an active edge and usable public void logic.
